title: rbac-v2: enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging + data residency controls
author: Ethan Kim
ci_checks: ci/integration - failed (flaky test: audit-logger-ttl) on first run, retried and passed
release_notes: Enforce KMS region pinning for RBAC v2 resources; audit logging enhancements for residency policy actions; backward-compatible migration path and rollout plan.
description:
Motivation: customers require deterministic data residency and KMS key residency controls tied to RBAC policies. This PR enforces KMS region pinning for RBAC v2 resources, improves audit logging for residency and key-binding actions, and adds a migration path so existing policies are validated and optionally auto-corrected.

Summary of changes: adds enforcement logic in the RBAC policy evaluator to validate kms_region against resource residency constraints; surfaces audit events for policy-create/update/delete that include residency and key metadata; introduces a config flag `rbac.v2.enforce_kms_region_pinning` (default: false) with a rollout path; new validation error codes and user-facing messages; migration job to scan existing policies and emit suggested changes (and a dry-run patch output).

Checklist:
- [x] Core enforcement in rbac/evaluator
- [x] Audit logger: structured fields for kms_key, kms_region, residency_policy_id
- [x] Admin console: residency validation warnings (UI change in a follow-up PR)
- [x] Migration CLI job: `rbac migrate-kms-region-pin --dry-run`
- [x] Integration tests covering enforcement + audit events
- [x] Docs: compliance guide and release notes

Migration notes: default behavior is opt-in. Operators should run the migration job in dry-run mode to get a list of policies that violate new constraints. The migration job supports `--fix` which will create suggested patches; fixes are additive and safe but require admin review. Rolling out `rbac.v2.enforce_kms_region_pinning=true` will cause policy create/update requests that violate residency/KMS constraints to be rejected with error code RBAC_KMS_REGION_PINNING_VIOLATION.

Testing: added unit tests for the evaluator and audit logger, integration test that exercises a simulated policy create/update across region-bound KMS keys, and an end-to-end test verifying the migration job output. CI initially surfaced a flaky audit TTL test which was stabilized by waiting for background retention to complete; CI rerun passed.

Impact: enforces data residency and KMS key residency constraints at policy evaluation time to prevent accidental cross-region key binding. Administrators can opt-in gradually and use migration tooling to remediate.
